paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Paul boasts, but he says he's speaking "as a fool" (2 Corinthians 11:17), and then he picks the weirdest things to brag about. Beatings, shipwrecks, nights without sleep, and a daily "concern for all the churches" (2 Corinthians 11:28). If I'd been handed the mic, I'd have led with my best cookie. Paul leads with his bruises.

That's the whole lesson, baker: "If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness" (2 Corinthians 11:30). Paul could match anyone on credentials, and he did, but the things he wanted people to see were the hard parts. And look at his heart, because he says, "Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?" (2 Corinthians 11:29). I think that tells us his sufferings weren't a trophy shelf. They came from loving people and serving Christ.

So what do you do with this? Next time you feel pressure to look impressive, remember the apostle who tells a story about leaving town in a basket (2 Corinthians 11:33). Your hard days, your rough edges and your most embarrassing chapters don't have to be hidden. Paul says they're worth talking about, so keep serving, keep loving people, and don't be shy about the basket.
